To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
loss of α‐catenin expression is associated with scattered cell growth and disruption of cell‐to‐cell contact in gastric and breast cancer.

the loss of expression of α catenin, an intracellular component of cell adhesion molecules, was frequent in scirrhoid adenocarcinoma of the stomach, which is a carcinoma with a scattered growth pattern.
the loss of expression of E‐cad and α catenin is a frequent event in gastric and breast cancers with scattered cell growth, and that this loss of expression is not organ specific.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the loss of α‐catenin expression, which is a key component of cell–cell adhesion.
the role of α catenin in the loss of cell‐cell adhesion in scirrhosis of the breast.
the mechanisms of disruption in cell adhesion in scirrhos carcinomas with scattered cells growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
loss of α catenins is a frequent and early event in human carcinogenesis.
α‐catenin expression is lost in scirrhosus carcinomas of the stomach.
the loss of α catenins and E‐cadherins are associated with the disruption of cell‐to‐cell adhesion and the acquisition of invasive potential in scirrhoid carcinomas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the disruption of E‐cad‐cadherin complex is one of the mechanisms for the invasion and metastasis of cancer cells.
loss of α catenins is an important mechanism of disruption of E‐cad‐herin‐based cell–cell adhesion, especially in carcinomas with scat‐tered cell growth.
the loss of α catenins is a frequent event in the carcinomas of the stomach, the breast and the prostate and that this event may play a critical role in carcinomas with a scattered cell growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
α catenin loss may be a more common event in scirrhosis than E‐cadherins loss.
the loss of α‐catenin is an important step in the development of scirrhous gastric cancer, and the loss of E‐cad is not.
α‐catenin is a potential biomarker for scirrhous gastric cancer, and it may also have prognostic value.
